frames.review_note: Minor only: Nagoji's pale ridged brand sits nearer the elbow than a hand's width above the wrist (small, not letters, acceptable at this distance); a thin dark teal strip shows under Ibrahim's shoulder cloth beside the vest (reads as cloth lining, not a coat); Ibrahim is front-lit rather than backlit in the doorway; his scar has a faint pink tint but reads pale. Otherwise clean: hut interior with hearth smoke, slatted window, mat and gruel bowl; healer with grey-streaked low knot and undyed cloth over both shoulders, no blouse or gold; Ibrahim in cream pocketed vest, white shirt, striped shoulder cloth, white mundu, no coat, bare forehead; Nagoji bare-chested, moustache, clean chin, gold stud, rope burns, linen only on hands, ankle chafe; no fishermen, no text. Plain mud wall between the window and the door post above Nagoji holds both captions.

Acceptable, minor notes only. (1) The brand is a pale, crackled patch of raised ridges a hand's width above the linen-wrapped wrist, with no letters, numerals or cross, and it is not red. But because the bandaged hand rests on the knee, the surface we see reads more like the top of the forearm than its inner side. (2) Long faint pinkish healed scar lines cross Nagoji's back and upper arm; the script lists rope burns on the chest only. This is not gore. (3) Ibrahim's scar is a thin pinkish-red line on his LEFT cheek, matching his approved sheet rather than the script's 'bare pale line'. (4) Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold ball, not a stud (author undecided, not a reason to reject). Clean otherwise: correct hut interior (mud wall, thatch, barred window, clay pots, open clay lamp, no fort or harbour). It is an over-the-LEFT-shoulder shot with the wrapped hand on his knee at the frame edge. Ibrahim wears the cream pocketed vest, white shirt, striped shoulder cloth and white turban, with a grey-flecked beard, no coat and a bare forehead, and his eyes are on the forearm. No text anywhere. Lettering space: plain mud wall between Ibrahim's turban and Nagoji's hair (x 0.47-0.66, y 0.03-0.45) and the upper-left wall beside the window (x 0.08-0.28, y 0.03-0.28). v01 is still the outdoor fort quay with an iron ring and rope, so it is rejected.

The round-3 fix landed. The scar on Ibrahim's LEFT cheek is no longer the glossy orange-red line with bright highlights that made v02 read as a fresh cut. It is now a thin, matte, pale grey line that runs as a narrow parting through the grey-flecked beard, from below the left ear to the jaw, and reads as an old healed scar. Nothing else changed in a meaningful way (the differences from v02 are small and confined to the face). The composition, the hut interior with the beach doorway, the open brass bowl oil lamp (no glass), the white turban, the cream vest over a white shirt (no teal coat) and the bare forehead (no ash) are all kept. His LEFT hand rises from his left side, with the thumb resting just under the left ear at the top of the scar, so the gesture flows into 1.5. The hand is anatomically sound. There is no text, no European element and no noose. The plain wall at the top left and the large plain wall at the upper right give clear space for the caption and both balloons. Notes only: (a) The healed scar now has a slight grey-mauve tone and is paler than the pinkish scar in panels 1.2 and 1.3. That is acceptable, but a later pass could even the scar tone across the page. (b) The boat in the doorway is a blurred single-masted local craft on the beach, not a European ship. (c) His beard reads a little fuller than 'short'. v02 is not a usable backup because its red, glossy scar reads as a fresh wound.

Acceptable, with these notes. (1) Hand continuity: his thumb rests on the scar, but it is his RIGHT hand crossing his chest, while panel 1.4 (and the round-1 correction for this panel) use the LEFT hand from the near side. The gesture therefore switches hands between consecutive panels; the script beat ('thumb has stopped on the scar') still reads. (2) His eyes drift up and toward screen right, away from Nagoji, rather than toward a doorway beyond the left edge. The 'somewhere else' beat still lands. (3) He looks seated rather than crouched on his heels as in 1.2 and 2.1. (4) Nagoji's soft-focus head and back fill the left ~40%, so Ibrahim's face is the focal point but not literally the largest thing. (5) There are long reddish healed rope-burn lines on Nagoji's back (not gore). (6) Nagoji's ear ornament is a hanging gold ball (author undecided, not a reason to reject). Clean otherwise: hut interior with mud wall, thatch and an open brass oil lamp, and no stone, ring, rope, fort or ships. The scar is a pale healed line on Ibrahim's LEFT cheek. He wears the vest, white shirt and striped shoulder cloth, with no coat and a bare forehead. Nagoji is bare-shouldered, in lost profile with the moustache tip. No text. Both lettering lines fit on Nagoji's side, on the plain mud wall at x 0.25-0.6, y 0.02-0.45, clear of Ibrahim's face. v01 is still the stone room opening onto a harbour with a European tower and galleons, so it is rejected.

Minor only. Ibrahim is still crouched at the mat's edge in a dim hut interior (plaster wall, wooden posts, woven mat, open-flame brass lamp, no glass). His costume is right: cream pocketed vest over a white shirt, white mundu, white turban, grey-flecked beard, blue-striped shoulder cloth, no teal coat and no ash. The scar is on his anatomical LEFT, since he faces screen left. Nagoji appears only as a soft, faceless bare shoulder at the left edge, as the audit allowed. The scar is drawn reddish like the sheet, not pale. His expression is more a sceptical frown than a suppressed smile. He wears sandals indoors. The upper-left wall (x 0.05-0.35, y 0.02-0.28) and the upper-right wall (x 0.57-0.86, y 0.02-0.38) are clear for both balloons.

v02 is clean. It fixes the setting: an indoor thatched mud hut with a slatted window, clay pots and hearth smoke. The healer is at screen left, heavy-set, with a grey-streaked low knot, undyed cotton over both shoulders, no blouse, no gold, hands on hips and a betel tint on her lips only. Nagoji sits on the mat in the centre. Ibrahim crouches at screen right with his LEFT cheek to camera and the scar on that side. He has no coat, a cream vest over a white shirt and no ash. Minor notes: Ibrahim's scar is drawn reddish rather than pale, but it matches his sheet. There are faint skin highlights on his forehead that do not read as ash. His gaze is horizontal toward Nagoji and the healer together, so the 'without looking at her' beat is only implied. Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, not a stud (noted only, as the author asked). v01 is still unacceptable: stone masonry, a post with an iron ring, rope, barrels and a painted border.

v02 is acceptable. It is the same thatched mud hut with a wooden slatted window and clay pots, and only Ibrahim and Nagoji are in frame. Ibrahim is half risen with one hand on his knee and turns toward Nagoji, his LEFT cheek and scar to camera. He has no coat, the cream pocketed vest, the blue-striped shoulder cloth and no ash. Nagoji is bare-chested in the captivity dhoti, with a clean chin, a moustache and linen-wrapped hands, and his inner left forearm turned down. Hands are sound. The plain mud wall in the upper centre has clear room for both balloons. Minor notes: the hut's right side opens under the eave onto a grove with palms and a fence, like a verandah, which is acceptable for a Kerala hut but less enclosed than 2.2. Ibrahim's expression is more wary than mild. Nagoji's ear ornament is a hanging gold drop (noted only). v01 is still unacceptable: a Portuguese soldier with a morion and pike, stone walls, an iron ring with rope, and a painted border.

Minor only. This is a strong echo of Chapter 1, 6.5: the black mare's head, neck and wind-tossed mane in misty dawn light over water at screen left. It dissolves into ragged ink splatter with no border. Nagoji's still face sits at centre-right: bare-shouldered, hair loose, thick curled moustache, clean chin with light stubble. The cracked hut wall and wooden-slatted window behind him fit the house. There is no text. The ear ornament is a tiny two-bead drop rather than a flush stud, but it reads as a small stud at panel size. The mare has a small pale forehead mark, which matches the front view on her sheet. The healing marks on his shoulder are faint, not gore.

Minor only. Nagoji's collarless tunic shows two tiny buttons at the neck slit (script says no buttons). Ibrahim walks beside Nagoji rather than clearly leading. Ibrahim's LEFT-cheek scar is not readable at this size. The net-mender looks toward the travellers rather than down the path to the sea. Otherwise clean: Nagoji has the moustache, clean chin, gold stud, tied-back hair, bare feet and linen-wrapped wrists. Ibrahim wears the pocketed vest, white mundu and turban with no teal coat and no ash. The well, children and net-menders are present, there is no text, and clear sky at top centre (x 0.42-0.68, y 0-0.12) holds the caption.

v02 is acceptable. It is the corrected wide shot: both men are small on a raised bund between flooded paddy, Ibrahim leads and Nagoji walks behind with his head turned aside. Nagoji is barefoot with linen-wrapped wrists, a moustache, a clean chin and his hair tied back. Ibrahim wears a white turban, a grey-flecked beard, the cream pocketed vest over a white shirt and a white mundu, with no coat and no forehead marks. There are thatched or tiled Kerala houses in the background and no European elements. The whole upper half is clear sky for both balloons. Minor points: Nagoji's tunic shows a short buttoned placket, though at this scale it reads like the 3.1 tunic. The low sun disc on the horizon makes this a sunset ('darkening sky', as the script asks), a lighting jump from the daylight 3.3 and 3.4 frames. v01 is not a backup: the figures are large, not small in frame, and Nagoji wears sandals.

Acceptable, with these notes. The sky is bright midday blue, while 3.2 calls for a darkening sky; this is close to panels 1 and 4, but the 3.2 correction asks for late-afternoon light to bridge the gap. A small crenellated hill fort sits on the far hill at top left (x 0.05-0.15, y 0.16-0.22), likely bleeding in from the reference sheet's Deccan backdrop. It is period-plausible but unscripted, and the top-left caption may cover it. Nagoji is seated, where 3.2 has him walking. There is light stubble on his jaw, which is allowed just after captivity. His likeness is strong: thick curled moustache, gold stud, collarless tunic with no buttons, linen-wrapped wrists, eyes closed, breathing in. Pepper vines with berry spikes climb the support tree at right. There is no text, and the clear sky band across the top holds all three lettering areas.

Minor only. The carter has a faint thin moustache, though the script says clean-shaven; he is not a principal, but later carter panels should follow one look. The light is bright daytime rather than late afternoon. A small whitewashed church with a bell tower sits on the distant shore, which is period-plausible. Ibrahim's LEFT scar is faint. The script beat is fully met: an open two-wheeled cart with spoked wheels and no hood, two white bullocks under a yoke, and a thin bare-chested carter with a topknot and goad stick at the yoke. The plain unmarked sacks and palm-leaf baskets are there, one sack open on wrinkled black peppercorns, and Ibrahim (vest, no coat, no ash) rests his hand in it. Nagoji stands at the left edge with tied-back hair, gold stud and a bandaged wrist. There is no text, and the sky from x 0.45 to 0.85, y 0.02 to 0.25 is clear for both balloons.

Accepted fault for the author list: Ibrahim still shows a faint diagonal scar mark on his RIGHT cheek (the image-left side of his face, in front of his visible ear). The v03 edit made it lighter than in v02, but it was not removed, and the LEFT-side scar is not shown. Everything else is clean. The setting is right: an inland red-earth clearing with palms and hills, no harbour or ships. Ibrahim wears the cream pocketed vest over a white shirt with a white mundu and white turban, has his short grey-flecked beard, and his forehead is bare, which is correct before 5.3. The open spoked cart and the two pale bullocks are there. The v03 edit fixed the carter: he is now clean-shaven and holds a goad stick, so v03 is clearly better than v02. There is no text or gore and the hands are sound. Minor notes, none of them grounds for rejection: Nagoji is seen from behind in lost profile, so only his moustache tip, ear and a small gold drop earring show and the chin cannot be checked; his linen wraps cover the wrists rather than the whole hands. There is clear sky at upper centre-right, between the tree canopy and the palms, for his one balloon. At 1536x1024 the frame will need the 2x upscale for print.

Fix landed: the pink line on Ibrahim's near (RIGHT) cheek in v02 is gone; v03's near cheek and beard are plain, unmarked skin. His far LEFT cheek is hidden by the turn of his head, so no scar shows, which the edit allowed. Nothing else got worse. On model: white turban, short grey-flecked beard, cream pocketed vest over a white shirt, white mundu and a striped shoulder cloth. There is no teal coat and no ash on his bare forehead. He does the careful shrug with a sidelong glance to screen left, toward Nagoji off-panel. The setting is a late-afternoon Kerala clearing by the cart, with sacks, a white bullock, paddy and thatched houses. There is no European element. Both open hands are anatomically sound. The edit moved the figure slightly left of where v02 had him. That leaves a wide, clear golden sky at upper right and centre for both lettering lines. There is no text, pseudo-text or painted balloon. v02 stays rejected for the right-cheek scar, so there is no backup.

Acceptable. The setting is now correct: palms, paddy and open late-afternoon sky. There is no fort, church, soldier or building. Ibrahim is up on the open spoked cart with plain sacks: white turban, grey-flecked beard, cream pocketed vest over a white shirt, white mundu, no coat, bare forehead. The scar is on his LEFT cheek, by the ear at screen right. Nagoji is in the foreground, seen from behind and below: his RIGHT arm in the cream sleeve down to the linen wrap, curly hair gathered at the nape, thick moustache, light stubble, no brand. Upper-left sky is clear for both lines. Minor notes: (1) The scar is pinkish with a small crossing tick rather than fully pale. It matches the reddish scar on the character sheet. (2) Ibrahim's fist closes around Nagoji's fully wrapped hand, so Nagoji's fingers are hidden. It reads as a helping clasp, but it is not quite 'Nagoji's hand closing on it'. (3) Nagoji's ear ornament is a round gold stud with a slight drop; the author has not yet decided between stud and drop. (4) A thin painted black border runs around the frame; the panel border will cover it. v01 is still rejected: a Portuguese fort, church and helmeted soldiers.

Fixes landed. The white horizontal stripes on Ibrahim's forehead in v02 are fully painted out, leaving bare brown skin under the turban. His far eye keeps a small pale highlight, which reads at panel scale as a sideways glance, not a blank eye (minor). The carter's droopy moustache is removed; only a faint mouth-corner shadow remains, and his upper lip reads as clean-shaven at panel size. The composition, sky, temple, deepastambham, fireflies, cart and bullocks are unchanged from v02, so nothing got worse. On model: Nagoji has the thick curled moustache, a clean chin and the collarless cream tunic, with his wrists still bandaged. His hair is swept back to the nape and reads as tied back, though not crisply. His ear ornament is too small to see at this scale (note only). Ibrahim wears the white turban, grey-flecked beard and cream vest over a white shirt and white mundu, with no teal coat and no scar on his visible right cheek. The setting is Kerala: a dusk paddy road, open spoked cart with sacks, two pale humped bullocks, a bare-chested carter with a topknot and goad, and a low tiered tiled-roof temple with a brass lamp pillar and no tower. Nothing is European and there are no glass lanterns. The deep blue upper sky is clear for the small Ibrahim balloon. There is no text and no painted balloon. v02 stays rejected for the forehead stripes, so there is no backup.

Minor only. The scar from the LEFT ear to the jaw is a thin reddish line rather than a pale one, but it matches the reddish scar on the sheet and is on the correct cheek. A thin blue stripe runs along the edge of his mundu. With the bullock's horn at the lower left, the lamp hangs from a rear or side rail behind him rather than the front rail. None of this matters at panel size. The correction worked: the harbour, ships and fort are gone. He now sits up on the grain sacks over wet paddy fields, with a red-earth track, coconut palms and low hills against the last deep blue sky and a thin orange horizon. He is in profile facing screen left with the scar toward the camera, wearing the white turban, the grey-flecked beard and the cream pocketed vest over a white shirt, with no coat and a bare forehead. The lamp is the open brass bowl on chains with a lit wick. The hands are sound and there is no text. v01 still shows the harbour and fort, so it stays rejected. The upper-left sky is empty and low-detail for the balloon.

Minor only. Nagoji's hair looks mostly loose behind his shoulders rather than clearly tied back. One woman in the far-left doorway seems to wear a red fitted upper garment under her white wrap. A distant lit silhouette at the centre horizon could read as a towered temple. Everything required is right: open clay lamps in the doorways; the cart lamp is an open brass bowl on chains; bare-chested boys in loincloths, with the pointing boy's face visible and his arm aimed at the men on the sacks; Nagoji has the moustache, clean chin, gold stud, cream tunic-shirt and bandaged wrists; Ibrahim has no coat and no ash and calls back over his shoulder; the carter is right. The sky in the upper left and centre has room for both balloons.

Nagoji's small gold ear stud is missing: his ear is visible and the lobe is bare. He is a small background figure, so this is barely noticeable, but it could be retouched in. No carter is drawn, and Nagoji holds the reins. Everything else is right: the shrine under a tree hung with cloth strips and bangles, a small open clay lamp at the stone image, an old woman in a white wrap over both shoulders with no blouse pressing one grey-white thumb smear of ash onto Ibrahim's forehead while she looks up and past him toward the cart, Ibrahim offering a coin, his LEFT-cheek scar showing, no coat, the cart's hanging brass lamp with an open flame and no glass. The sky in the upper centre-right is clear for the balloon.

Fix landed. The two crisp white horizontal stripes on Ibrahim's forehead in v02 are gone. v03 shows one soft-edged, grey-white thumb smear of ash in the centre of the forehead just below the turban, with no lines, dot or red paste. A pixel diff shows nothing else changed meaningfully. Composition, the brass hanging open-wick lamp, the tree with cloth strips, the red-earth road, paddy and palms, the white bullocks and both poses are identical to v02. Ibrahim is on model: white turban, short grey-flecked beard, cream pocketed vest over a white shirt, white mundu and striped shoulder cloth, no teal coat. His scar runs from the LEFT ear to the jaw, and the right cheek is clean. Note: the scar is drawn as a thin pinkish-red line, as on the character sheet, rather than a pale one. It is not gory. Nagoji has the thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, the cream collarless tunic and bandaged wrists, and a skeptical raised brow. His hair is gathered back, with curls loose at the sides. Note only: his ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, not a stud. Both men's hands are sound. There is no text, pseudo-text, glass lantern or European element. The upper-right sky is large, clear and low-detail, with room for both Ibrahim balloons. Minor continuity note: the small stone shrine house behind them differs slightly from 5.3's stone image at the tree base, but the tree, lamp and bullocks match. v02 stays rejected for the forehead stripes.

Clean pick. Dusk bazaar, red stone compound wall and wooden gate, rutted earth. The cart has two pale grey humped bullocks, a thin bare-chested carter with a topknot, and a hanging brass lamp with an open wick. Two Nair guards in white jackets, sashes and topknots, with spears and round shields and no turbans. The speaking guard (left) faces the cart. Ibrahim matches: white turban, grey-flecked beard, cream pocketed vest over a white shirt, white mundu, no coat. Nagoji matches: hair tied back, thick moustache, clean chin, gold stud, cream tunic-shirt, bandaged wrists. Every lamp is an open brass lamp. The open sky above the wall at top centre has room for both balloons. Minor: no ash is visible on Ibrahim's forehead (allowed, since the chapter check forbids ash). The far lights inside the compound are soft glows, not lanterns you can read as such. Panels 6.2 to 6.5 must be regenerated to match this dusk, lamp-lit setting.

Clean pick; the correction worked. It is deep blue dusk at the red laterite compound wall and wooden gate, lit by open brass niche lamps, with no sea, fort or church. Nagoji sits high on the sacks in the same spoked bullock cart as 6.1, with the grey humped bullocks partly in frame. The Nair guard (white jacket, sash, topknot, spear, round shield, no turban) looks up at him. Ibrahim stands at the front of the cart and jerks his thumb toward Nagoji. He faces screen left, so the pale scar shows on his LEFT cheek. He wears the cream pocketed vest over a white shirt, white mundu and striped shoulder cloth, with no coat. Nagoji has a thick curled moustache, a clean chin, hair tied at the nape, bandaged wrists and the cream tunic. Minor notes: (1) Ibrahim's ash is two or three short, smudged horizontal streaks rather than the single thumb smear of 5.3. It is faint, but a retouch into one smear would match 5.3 and 5.4. (2) Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging drop, not a stud (author undecided). (3) His tunic has a short buttoned placket, against the 'no buttons' lock, as in the accepted 6.1 and 5.3. (4) The cart lamp is an open-wick brass bowl hung from a cap on two thin rods. The wall shows clearly between the rods, so it reads as brass, not a glass chimney. Lettering: Ibrahim's two balloons fit the clear night sky upper right; the guard's fits the dark sky upper left, above the wall.

Accepted faults for the author's list (v03, the latest edit, is v02 with these marks only slightly softened): (1) Ibrahim's forehead ash still reads as three soft horizontal white stripes just below the turban, not one thumb smear. (2) The seated official on the far platform still has a small dark-red dot at the centre of his forehead; the script says no forehead marks. (3) Minor: Ibrahim's scar is a thin pale line on his visible LEFT cheek that runs from below the ear toward the corner of the moustache rather than down to the jaw. It is on the correct side. Everything else is clean. The setting is right: a night hall with carved wooden pillars, open brass oil lamps on chains and on stands, a packed-earth floor and a mat, bare-chested Nair men in topknots turned toward the official, and guards in white mundu with crossed belts. Ibrahim (white turban, grey-flecked beard, cream pocketed vest over a white shirt, no teal coat) whispers behind a cupped hand into Nagoji's ear. Nagoji has a thick curled moustache, a clean chin, a small gold ear drop, hair tied back, the cream tunic-shirt and bandaged hands. There is no painted text, and the palm leaves are blank. Lettering can go in the rafters across the top right (x 0.45 to 0.92, y 0 to 0.14) and on the plain back wall above the official (x 0.62 to 0.88, y 0.18 to 0.31).

Clean pick; the correction worked. It is drawn in the inked, coloured graphic-novel style of 6.3 and 6.4, not photorealistic. It is the same night hall: dark wooden pillars, open brass oil lamps on chains and a brass standing lamp, with no daylight, palms or doorway. The official sits cross-legged on his low platform on a woven mat, with no chair or desk. He has a heavy round face, a grey Kerala topknot, a greying moustache, a clean chin, a bare torso and a plain white shoulder cloth. There is no forehead mark, chain or thread, and he matches 6.4 v02. A thin iron stylus works a single blank palm-leaf strip with a string hole, with no pen, ink or paper. His eyes look up toward the viewer's left, where the stranger stands. The stranger is only an out-of-focus edge of cream cloth at the left, with no face or beard. The single background guard is bare-headed with a topknot. Minor notes: (1) The frame is portrait (1024x1536), unlike the landscape v01. The layout crops toward the slot and keeps the face zones. (2) The stylus tip rests on the leaf rather than hovering just above it. Lettering: the plain dark wall upper right, between the two hanging lamps and above his head, takes the one small balloon.

Accepted faults for the author list. (1) Ibrahim still has two short pale-white dashes on his RIGHT cheek (screen-left, just below the eye). The v03 edit did not remove them. (2) His forehead ash is a small pale rectangular patch with faint horizontal striping, just below the turban, not one soft thumb smear. This is better than v02's two distinct white stripes but still not a smear. Everything else is clean. It is the same lamp-lit Travancore hall, with carved pillars, open brass oil lamps on chains, a packed-earth floor and seated bare-chested Nair men in white mundus with topknots. The official's platform edge, arm and palm-leaf bundle are at the right, with dusk palms and a tiled roof through the open side. There is nothing European. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear drop, collarless cream tunic over a dhoti, bandaged hands clasped, barefoot, upright. Ibrahim is half a step behind at his shoulder, in a cream pocketed vest over a white shirt and white mundu, with a white turban, grey-flecked beard and sandals, and no teal coat. There is no painted text, no balloons and no gore, and the hands are sound. Lettering space: the large shadowed wall at upper right (roughly x 0.50-0.88, y 0.05-0.40) is clear for both the caption and Nagoji's balloon, and the beams at top left can take the caption if needed. Note: the contact-sheet tile labelled v02 shows a different, more centred composition than the v02 frame file. The frame files for v02 and v03 share the same composition, so the frame files were used here.

Acceptable. It is a single full-frame close-up with no inset. An older man's bare, hairy brown hand cuts a few abstract scratches into a corded palm-leaf bundle; the strokes do not form any legible script. Lighting is an open brass oil lamp, and the upper third is a plain grey wall with room for both lettering lines. Minor points: the rendering is photographic rather than the inked line-and-wash of 7.1, 7.3 and 7.4, and the top leaf reads slightly like a wooden board.

Clean pick; both parts of the r3 fix landed and nothing got worse. (1) The plain round neckline of the collarless cream homespun tunic now shows along the bottom edge and covers both shoulders, with no collar or buttons, so no bare shoulder or chest is visible. (2) The hair is swept back behind the ears and gathered into a low bunch of curls at the nape that ends above the neckline. A few curls fall at the temple and forehead, and nothing hangs loose to the shoulders. The light is warmer amber. Identity matches the sheet: strong cheekbones, straight nose, thick curled moustache, clean chin with light stubble at most, and a small flush gold stud (not a drop). The background is the same hall: an out-of-focus dark carved pillar, a plain wall and an open brass oil lamp on a chain, with no glass, sky or fort. The expression is steady and level, with a slight upward gaze toward the platform; it reads as flat and certain. Minor: the framing is a head-and-neck close-up rather than a tight crop on the eyes, which is acceptable. There is no text. The plain wall at upper right (x 0.62 to 0.86, y 0.04 to 0.42), clear of the lamp, takes the one balloon.

The r3 fix landed. The background is now the closed evening hall: carved dark wooden pillars, dim warm walls, and open brass oil lamps hanging on chains and on stands. There is no colonnade, balustrade, sky, palms or daylight. Both guards and their brass helmets are gone. There is no turbaned bearded man and no European in a coat. The official is kept as drawn: older and heavy, in profile, grey-streaked Kerala topknot, greying moustache, clean chin, bare torso, plain white shoulder cloth. His stylus is lifted clear of a blank palm-leaf strip on its wooden rest, and the first trace of a smile shows. The palm-leaf bundle, brass pot and standing lamp at left are kept in the same inked style. The hand holding the stylus is anatomically sound. There is no text or pseudo-script, and none is needed. The lighting and rendering match 8.1 v03. Minor notes: (1) Four bare-chested seated men sit cross-legged on mats in white mundus with topknots. The leftmost has a short full beard, and the second has stubble and somewhat lighter brown skin, although the prompt asked for clean chins. Neither reads as European or as Ibrahim, and 8.1 v03 also seats bearded elders. (2) The seated men look toward screen right at the official, not toward the off-panel Nagoji at screen left. That still plays the beat: in the silence, every eye is on the official's reaction. (3) The lidded brass pot could be read as an inkwell, as in earlier accepted panels. v02 is still unacceptable because of its daylight colonnade and helmeted guards.

Clean, with minor notes. Night under moonlight only, with no lamps and no glass. Nagoji sleeps on a woven mat by the veranda post under the eaves, in the cream tunic-shirt and dhoti, with a thick curled moustache, a clean chin with only light stubble and a small gold ear stud. The bandaged near hand lies loosely curled on the mat. Beyond him are the red laterite wall, pepper vines on their support trees and the pale road running away into the dark. There is no text or pseudo-text, and the anatomy is sound. Minor: his hair is spread behind his head on the pillow rather than clearly tied back, which is natural for sleep.
